contract: A wait's deadline at D runs only once its customer's input watermark W has passed D. W is worked out afresh each time a deadline asks: it is now, or just before the earliest input of that customer the device has already captured but not yet committed and readable, for example a renderer emission waiting in staging. An input at exactly D is in time, because the wait window is inclusive, so it holds D. Once W has passed D, every committed input of that customer that happened at or before D is delivered first, in occurrence order, through the ordinary event path; then the deadline runs against whatever checkpoint results, and that answer is final. Only events already committed when the deadline reaches the front of the queue count; an event committed after the deadline has run stays late and does not reopen the wait. An input the device had not captured when the deadline ran, such as a backdated event arriving afterwards, is late too. A staged input holds W for at most the staging bound, stagingBoundMillis, the renderer flush interval, timed on a monotonic clock; a tap staged longer than that is late. While the customer's recovery is pending, or a read of their committed inputs has failed, W does not advance: their deadlines wait, asked again only by the queue's one retry timer, until the read succeeds. A waiting deadline holds back only its own Journey's inputs that happened after D. Other Journeys, other customers and the customer's other entries keep flowing, and a competing trigger from another Journey is judged when it is captured. On sign-in, captured inputs move with the customer to the identified customer.
